image_description: A close-up, top-down view of a chiton (marine mollusk) clinging to a rough, wet rock surface. The chiton has an elongated oval shape with eight distinct, overlapping dorsal plates (valves) that are light beige/cream colored with darker mottling. These plates are surrounded by a textured, leathery girdle that matches the color of the surrounding rock and algae. The background consists of dark, wet stone with some small barnacles or other marine encrustations visible.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The texture of the chiton's girdle blends very smoothly into the surrounding rock/algae. While this could be camouflage, the lack of any distinct edge shadow or separation suggests slight 'melting' or failure to define the object boundary distinctly from the background.
The overlaps between the calcareous plates are somewhat soft and lack the sharp, hard-edged definition expected of calcified structures. They appear slightly rubbery rather than rigid.
